note: A source declaration on a pooled edition loses to explicit coverage, as in occurrence resolution (Y-202): it binds only the years no explicit occurrence of its column covers, so the explicit year keeps its own declaration and evidence. The one build route to a pooled declaration beside an explicit one on one column is an [[errata.column]] naming both a pooled and an annual edition in `versions` (scb_errata.py `convert_column_entry`: one addition per named edition, each with its edition's scope, all declaring the entry's one `classification`). One entry carries one book, so the replaced test's two contrary books (b pooled, a in 2017, and `multiple_classifications_declared` when unclipped) have no build shape; the same clip is observable here in the 2017 warning's refs. A [[coding.documented]] list gives the column a code 9 that book a lacks, so each bound state warns `nonconforming_classification_codes` citing its binding's evidence.
fails_if: `_source_bindings` (source_classification_bindings.py) binds a pooled declaration over its whole pooled range instead of the `_binding_bounds` clip (the declaration site back to `occurrence_bounds`), so the 2017 warning also cites the pooled edition 1618; or the clip drops the pooled declaration on the years it alone covers, so 2016 or 2018 loses 'a' and its warning

sources.description: SCB register 1 (variant 10) delivers VALUE in the pooled edition '2016 - 2018' (1618, member 1011) and the explicit 2017 (2017, member 1012). The curation adds column DECL by [[errata.column]] in both editions, declaring book A, with a documented list {1 One, 9 Nine} over 2016-2018. Book a has code 1 only.
